title: Stop stalled agents early instead of burning the full deadline
summary: The agent driver (crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs) only enforces a fixed wall-clock deadline and has no progress tracking, so a stalled producer burns the full 1800s before the job learns it. Add a stall watchdog in the driver: if the agent's stream shows no activity for a fraction of the timeout, kill it and report a timed-out outcome whose reason says it stalled. The existing timed-out work-keeping path (keep_timed_out_work) then preserves the partial work. Audience: Athena maintainers and the verifier.

defaults_applied.how: New stall tests plus workspace cargo test and clippy criteria.
Fix in the shared driver loop, not per job or role.
Tests run a hanging stand-in and check the early timed-out outcome.
One focused change in the driver.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy, and fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Root cause: the driver loop in claude.rs checks only Instant::now() >= clock + spec.timeout, with no notion of progress, so stalled and slow producers are indistinguishable until the full deadline.
Work retention on timeout already exists (keep_timed_out_work, TimedOut outcome, athena retry seeding), so the missing piece is early detection, not resumability.

Progress is read as any new stream-json line from the agent; the stall window is derived from spec.timeout (about one third, with a floor) so no AgentInvocation field is added and every role benefits.
Stalled kills reuse InvocationOutcome::TimedOut with a distinct 'stalled' detail so downstream handling stays the same.
No change to athena.toml or defaults.toml is needed.

acceptance_criteria.text: The change description names the root cause: the driver enforces only a fixed wall-clock deadline and never tracks progress, so a stalled agent is indistinguishable from a slow one.

A new test in crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs runs a stand-in agent that emits nothing and hangs, with a long timeout. It asserts the driver ends it well before the deadline, with outcome TimedOut and a detail that says it stalled. It fails on the base commit and passes with the change. Run: cargo test -p athena-agent.

A test shows an agent that keeps emitting stream lines past the stall window is not killed early, and the existing deadline test (detail 'deadline of 2s reached') still passes. Run: cargo test -p athena-agent.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets, and cargo test --workspace all pass.
The stall rule is implemented once in the shared driver loop, not per role or per job, so every agent role gets it.

out_of_scope: Splitting jobs into sub-jobs in planning
Changing the configured producer timeout values
Changing records/ or past job outcomes
urgent_reason: Cuts wasted time: producers that stall now stop early instead of burning the full 1800s deadline, which caused 9 failures in 8 jobs.
